strategy.headline: Philly loves a Sixer who earns it. Build from the gym, the order counter and Broad Street, not 1776.
strategy.thesis: Philadelphia loves the Sixers like a family it argues with, and its icons are adopted sons who ground it out. Stars who look like passengers get booed, so a LeBron James and Jaylen Brown superteam has to earn the city before the city makes it personal. Most of its heroes wear other brands: Iverson is Reebok, Embiid moved to Skechers, Brown runs 741 and Mitchell & Ness owns the replica throwback. Nike's own lanes are LeBron, Kobe's Lower Merion roots, Dr. J's Converse lineage, the team uniform (Specter included) and the gym credibility of the Palestra and the Sonny Hill League. Stock deep for the debut and save the Philly pieces for real wins. Speak the codes locals use with each other: the area code, "maneto," the order counter. Pay Philly hands to make the product, from North Philly letterers to North 5th Street designers.

archetype.name: The Prove-It Family
archetype.description: Suspicious by default, ride-or-die once a player bleeds for the city. Booing is accountability, and out-of-town grinders like Iverson and Kelce get adopted for life.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 45-37 Play-In season, Philly came back from 3-1 down against No. 2 Boston, then got swept in the second round by the eventual champion Knicks. Philly then traded Paul George for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join Embiid, Maxey and Edgecombe. Title odds moved to about +1000, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.
pulse.sentiment: Giddy but braced. The city knows three things decide the year: Embiid's availability, LeBron turning 42 in December and the fresh Knicks wound. It will judge both new stars on effort, not reputation.

topInsights.title: Philly's heroes wear other brands
topInsights.insight: The faces Philly wears most belong to other brands. Iverson is Reebok, Embiid is Skechers, Brown has his own 741 and Meek Mill is Puma. Philly-founded Mitchell & Ness, now under Fanatics, holds the replica throwback. Nike's own assets are LeBron, Kobe's Lower Merion roots, Converse's Dr. J Pro Leather lineage and the team uniform, Specter included.
topInsights.implication: Make LeBron, Kobe Day at Lower Merion and a Converse Dr. J tribute the hero stories. Meet the street's demand for Iverson-era black and red with an original black-red-gold layer: no name, no likeness, no Reebok cue. Stay out of the replica lane.

topInsights.title: Stock the debut, save the Philly pieces for the wins
topInsights.insight: This city booed Simmons and Harden and adopted Iverson and Kelce, and it greets a superteam with suspicion. Jersey and tee demand still peaks in the 72 hours around a debut. The fan underground (the Process bloggers, The Rights to Ricky Sanchez, local printers) answers every result with a one-color tee within hours.
topInsights.implication: Have name-and-number, Specter and layering product deep on shelves for Oct 20. Release the Philly-specific pieces only after real milestones: the first home win, the first win over the Knicks, Brown's Jan 21 return to Boston. For quick-turn tees, pay and credit a few local printers rather than trying to out-bootleg them.

topInsights.title: Spectrum '83 stands beside Specter
topInsights.insight: The 2030 arena will rise on the Spectrum site, home of Dr. J, Moses Malone and the 1983 title. This season Philly is also one of eight historic franchises in Nike's national Specter uniform program. Specter's Philly design and game dates aren't public yet, and Flyers fans share the Spectrum nostalgia.
topInsights.implication: Build a Spectrum '83 nostalgia layer that stands on its own: the 1983 banner, the building's outline, neon-sign vernacular. Clear it with the Sixers and Comcast Spectacor, and let it sit next to Specter merchandise without depending on it. Keep the new arena quiet until a groundbreaking.

topInsights.title: Insider codes beat landmarks, and 1776 is spent
topInsights.insight: Locals signal belonging through codes: "Whiz wit," the roast pork Italian, the area codes (215, 610, 856), "Philadelphia maneto," Billy Penn's hat and the tall "wickets" handstyle. After the 2026 Semiquincentennial summer, Liberty Bell clip art, Rocky, "jawn" and cheesesteak graphics read as tourist merch. Local shops already print the order-counter jokes.
topInsights.implication: Use the shorthand sparingly. Make area-code numerals the hero, add a "maneto" neck tape, and keep order-counter type to hangtags, packaging and one tee. Leave the pregame bell to the team.

topInsights.title: A basketball city under a football town
topInsights.insight: The Eagles own the city's wallet from September to January, but the hoops lineage runs deeper. Think of the Palestra and the Big 5, Public League versus Catholic League, and the Sonny Hill and Baker summer leagues. Players get claimed by high school: Wilt at Overbrook, Staley at Dobbins, Kobe at Lower Merion. Neighborhood sneaker doors set the taste, not Center City.
topInsights.implication: Earn credibility in the gyms, with league uniforms and a few well-made court rebuilds. Show up for the Public and Catholic League playoffs in February and March, with girls' and women's hoops alongside the boys'. Seed product through neighborhood doors. Save the loudest Sixers drops for October, December and the post-football run from February to April.

topInsights.title: One fan base, two rivers, many home languages
topInsights.insight: The team trains in Camden, and South Jersey (856) and the 610 suburbs argue about whether they count as Philly. Clothing is tax-free in both states. Inside the city, North Philly's Puerto Rican and Dominican blocks along North 5th Street, South Philly's Mexican corridor and Southwest Philly's West African community are full-season fans. The brand gives them no Spanish-language or diaspora voice.
topInsights.implication: One good-better-best price ladder should run across the region, with modular area-code editions so 856 and 610 get their own piece. Add a community-led bilingual thread with Taller Puertorriqueño and West African and Cameroonian community groups. Run it all season, not only at the September parade.

topInsights.title: In Philly, the maker is part of the product
topInsights.insight: Philly's visual culture is commissioned and handmade. Mural Arts has made more than 4,000 walls through neighborhood design sessions. Sign-painted rooftops line the El, the Fabric Workshop makes artist textiles, and every Philly soul LP prints its credits.
topInsights.implication: Credit the maker on everything. Pay named Philly letterers for the numerals, including Black sign painters and type designers from North and West Philly. Add an original "session credits" block naming the roster and the artist, co-branded hangtags, and courts that stay maintained after the product sells out.

uniform.concept: Broad Street (proposed City Edition for 2027-28 at the earliest)
uniform.narrative: A proposal, not this season's uniform. Broad Street is the line Philly lives on. It runs from North Broad's Uptown Theater, the Met and Temple, past the Clef Club and CAPA, to Broad & Pattison. That is where the Sixers play and where the city floods after every title. The uniform reads as a route through the 20th-century, Black-led Philly that locals grew up with, not 1776. Have North and West Philly hands draw its heritage lettering. Verify the 2026-27 City Edition (not yet confirmed) and the Specter design before sharing it outside Nike.
motifs: A single vertical route line down the side panel, with station dots from North Broad to Broad & Pattison, drawn in-house with no SEPTA logo or map art
Art Deco marquee lettering with bulb-dot inlines, inspired by North Broad's theater facades but drawn as original type
Concentric ring waves as a tonal emboss, no bell picture
An original 'session credits' block listing the roster and the lettering artist, with no record-label or song references
uniform.typography: "Sixers" in original Deco marquee block letters with bulb-dot inlines. Commission them from a paid, credited group of Philly letterers that includes Black sign painters and type designers from North and West Philly. Numbers are tall and condensed, with wickets proportions and a sign-painter drop shadow in royal.
details: Side panel: orange route line with cream station dots. It's the only orange on the uniform, so it never reads as Flyers.
Waistband: bronze ring emboss with 'Philadelphia maneto' in a small engraved serif
Neck tape: 215 · 267 · 445 · 610 · 484 · 856, so the city, the suburbs and South Jersey are all on the collar
Interior hem: session-credit block naming the roster and the lettering artists
Court and community tie-in: a sideline route line that ends at a "Broad & Pattison" stop, plus a funded court or wall on North Broad with a North Broad arts partner
avoid: Liberty Bell clip art, the 13-star 1776 motif and colonial script. The franchise and the 2026 Semiquincentennial have used them up.
Repeating any shipped City Edition theme, including Boathouse Row, or colliding with the Philly Specter look
Rocky, LOVE sculpture letters, SEPTA logos or map art, PSFS initials, PIR or MFSB names, and the Divine Lorraine sign without owner and Peace Mission consent
Mummers characters, face paint or 'Golden Slippers', and any Chinatown imagery after the 76 Place fight
Kensington Avenue 'grit' imagery, an off-the-shelf graffiti font, and promising any artist a uniform credit before the NBA signs off

music.headline: Philly's sound runs from Gamble & Huff to Meek Mill, and the Sixers already own its bell
music.summary: Philly soul came out of Sigma Sound in the 1970s, cut by Gamble, Huff and Thom Bell. The city also built a DJ-first hip-hop scene that runs from Lady B to Meek Mill. The Sixers already plug in through the pregame Liberty Bell ritual and Meek's 'Dreams and Nightmares' intro. Make the bell and uncommitted local artists the voice of Philly product.

insights.title: Philly soul is the heritage to build on
insights.detail: Gamble & Huff's Philadelphia International Records (longtime home: 309 S. Broad) and its house band MFSB, 'Mother Father Sister Brother,' cut the O'Jays, Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes and Teddy Pendergrass at Sigma Sound on N. 12th St. 'TSOP' became the Soul Train theme. 'Love Is the Message' became a disco and house cornerstone. In 1979 Gamble, radio host Dyana Williams and Ed Wright won White House recognition for June as Black Music Month.
insights.implication: This is Philly's most ownable music story, and it is literally about brotherly love. Build a Black History Month game-night capsule and a June Black Music Month lifestyle drop on it. License catalog, marks and lyrics from the rights holders.

insights.title: The bell is the Sixers' instrument
insights.detail: A guest rings a replica Liberty Bell to open Sixers home games. On April 24, 2018, then-co-owner Michael Rubin's helicopter flew Meek Mill from his prison release straight to the arena to ring it before the Sixers closed out Miami. Meek's 'Dreams and Nightmares (Intro)' has since become the default soundtrack of Philly sports celebrations, from the Eagles' 2018 title run to Sixers playoff nights.
insights.implication: Make the bell the sound and look of Sixers music events. Have a local musician ring it on drop nights, and put bronze hardware and ring graphics on product. Start with the James-Brown home debut against Cleveland.

insights.title: Philly hip-hop is neighborhood-coded and DJ-first
insights.detail: The line runs from Lady B's 1979 'To the Beat Y'all' and Schoolly D's 1985 'P.S.K.' out of Parkside. It passes through West Philly's DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince, then reaches State Property, Meek Mill, Lil Uzi Vert (Francisville), Tierra Whack and Armani White (West Philly). Jeff and the Fresh Prince won the first rap Grammy and made the transformer scratch famous. Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith joined the Sixers' ownership group in 2011.
insights.implication: Locals rep blocks and sections, not an abstract 'Philly.' Credit every collab to a specific artist and neighborhood, and clear brand deals first. Philly's hoops-hip-hop icon, Allen Iverson, is Reebok for life.

insights.title: The Roots built a live-band city
insights.detail: Questlove and Black Thought met at the High School for Creative and Performing Arts (CAPA) on South Broad, where Boyz II Men also formed. The Roots' late-'90s jam sessions launched Jill Scott, Musiq Soulchild and Bilal, and Jazmine Sullivan carries the neo-soul line now. The Roots Picnic, running since 2008 and now staged in West Fairmount Park, is the city's flagship hip-hop and R&B weekend.
insights.implication: Philly prizes musicianship over hype. Use the Roots Picnic window (late May or early June) to preview next season's city product with live-band artists, and treat CAPA as a natural youth design and music partner.

insights.title: A jazz city with a Dr. J song
insights.detail: John Coltrane's rowhouse at 1511 N. 33rd St. in Strawberry Mansion is a National Historic Landmark. The Sun Ra Arkestra has worked out of a Germantown house since Sun Ra moved there in 1968. Philly saxophonist Grover Washington Jr. wrote 'Let It Flow (For Dr. J)' for his 1980 album Winelight.
insights.implication: Julius Erving's sneaker lineage is Converse, now part of Nike Inc. A 'Let It Flow' Pro Leather and Sixers warmup tribute is a Nike-family exclusive no rival can match, provided Erving and the Washington estate license it and share in it.

insights.title: The new arena goes back to a concert landmark
insights.detail: The privately funded arena unveiled in September 2026 will rise on the Spectrum site. The Spectrum was the Sixers' home through the 1983 title season, and generations of Philadelphians saw their first concerts there. It sits in the same South Philly sports complex where JFK Stadium hosted Live Aid's U.S. show in 1985.
insights.implication: The 2026-2030 build is a multi-season homecoming story. Make Spectrum-era concert-tee graphics and 1983 throwbacks, cleared with the team and Comcast Spectacor, which controls Spectrum branding.

insights.title: Mummers: the city's oldest sound, with baggage
insights.detail: Every New Year's Day the string bands (banjos, saxophones, glockenspiels) strut up Broad Street in sequins and ostrich plumes built all year in South Philly's Two Street clubhouses. The Fancy Brigades stage shows at the Convention Center. Blackface was banned only in 1964, racist and anti-LGBTQ skits have recurred since, and the theme song 'Oh! Dem Golden Slippers' is an 1879 minstrel-era tune.
insights.implication: The craft is a rich, unmistakably Philly material story for the game nearest Jan 1. Source it through commissioned costume makers, and keep parade characters and 'wench' imagery off product.

people.why: 'Whack World' (2018) is 15 one-minute songs with surreal, art-directed visuals. That makes her the city's most designer-minded artist and a natural graphics collaborator.

people.role: Afrofuturist big band based in Germantown since 1968

vocabulary.meaning: Philly's all-purpose noun for any thing, place or person. It's all over local rap, signage and merch.
The Sixers' pregame ritual: a guest rings a replica Liberty Bell to start the night.
'The Sound of Philadelphia,' MFSB's 1974 Soul Train theme and shorthand for the whole Gamble & Huff and Thom Bell era.
'Mother Father Sister Brother,' the Sigma Sound house band behind most Philly soul hits.
An elder who has seen it all and a young guy coming up. 'Bul' means a guy, heard in Philly rap and on every court.
Acting out of pocket or overreacting, as in 'you drawlin'.'
South 2nd Street in Pennsport, the Mummers' clubhouse strip and their New Year's afterparty.
'Oh! Dem Golden Slippers,' the Mummers' strutting anthem, an 1879 minstrel-era song by James A. Bland.

designCues.cue: Liberty Bell bronze
designCues.source: The replica Liberty Bell rung before every Sixers home game, cast after the 1753 original.
designCues.use: Use for zipper pulls, aglets, eyelets and metallic embroidery. The hex approximates the patina, so match it to a bronze plating standard.

designCues.cue: Gold lamé shine
designCues.source: The Sun Ra Arkestra's metallic stage robes and the gold sequins of Mummers string-band suits. Philly's two great costume traditions both shine gold.
designCues.use: Use as the single metallic in a City capsule, such as foil numbers or metallic thread on Sixers royal #006BB6. The hex approximates, so match with a foil standard.

designCues.cue: Broad Street Line orange
designCues.source: SEPTA's Broad Street subway runs under the city's music spine, from North Broad's Uptown Theater and the Met past PIR and CAPA to the arena at Broad & Pattison.
designCues.use: Use as a hit color on track-list graphics. The hex is approximate, and any SEPTA map art needs SEPTA's permission.

designCues.cue: Bell rings: concentric sound waves radiating from a cracked bell
designCues.source: The Sixers' pregame bell ritual. The Liberty Bell image itself is public domain.
designCues.use: Use as a chest or back graphic, a tonal emboss or a hangtag shape. Pair it with the team's licensed marks rather than inventing a new bell logo.

designCues.cue: MFSB liner-notes credit block
designCues.source: Sigma Sound's house band, 'Mother Father Sister Brother,' and the dense session credits on Philly soul LPs.
designCues.use: Print an interior credit block that lists the roster as a session band, 'Recorded live at Broad & Pattison.' Any PIR logo or song title needs a license.

designCues.cue: North Broad marquee lettering
designCues.source: The 1929 Art Deco facade of the Uptown Theater, the 'Apollo of Philadelphia' for soul revues, and the restored marquee of the Met.
designCues.use: Use Deco block letters with bulb-dot detailing for warmup chest type. Commission original lettering rather than tracing either building's sign.

designCues.cue: Mummers sequins, satin and plumes
designCues.source: Hand-sewn string-band and Fancy Brigade costumes built all year on Two Street.
designCues.use: Use flip-sequin patches, satin linings or a single plume-print panel, made with paid Mummers costume makers. Never use parade characters or face paint.

designCues.cue: Hand-made Afrofuturist sleeves
designCues.source: Sun Ra's self-released El Saturn records, many with hand-drawn or hand-painted covers by Arkestra members.
designCues.use: Commission new art with the Arkestra and its estate for a space-age graphic tee. Don't copy El Saturn covers or use Sun Ra's name without a license.

productHooks: A 'Ring the Bell' drop for the James-Brown home debut against Cleveland: a bronze-hardware shooting shirt with a concentric bell-ring graphic, plus a LeBron Philly colorway. A Philly musician (candidates: Questlove, Jill Scott, Tierra Whack) rings the bell and scores the launch film.

An 'Ain't No Stoppin' Us Now' playoff-push tee and hoodie for March-April, using McFadden & Whitehead's 1979 Philadelphia International anthem (lyric licensed from its publishers) as a nod to last spring's 3-1 comeback against Boston.

An MFSB 'liner notes' warmup for Black History Month game nights, re-released for June's Black Music Month. An interior credit block lists the roster as a session band. Launch it at the Clef Club or the Met with Philly string and horn players.

A Broad Street track-list tee co-designed with a local artist: the Uptown, the Met, 309 S. Broad, the Clef Club and CAPA, the Mummers route and the arena as 'Side A.' Print it in Broad Street Line orange and sell it at doors along Broad.

A 'Let It Flow' Dr. J Pro Leather with matching Sixers warmup, made with Converse (Nike Inc.) and licensed from Julius Erving and Grover Washington Jr.'s estate. Time it for a 1983-title anniversary or Spectrum heritage night.
A New Year's capsule (sequin-patch beanie, satin-lined warmup) made with Mummers string-band costume makers for the game nearest Jan 1. Pay the makers and keep parade characters off product.
watchouts: Brand conflicts are everywhere. Allen Iverson is Reebok for life, Joel Embiid moved to Skechers in 2024, Jaylen Brown has been building his own 741 brand and Meek Mill signed with Puma in 2018. LeBron James is Nike's signature asset on this roster. Confirm every player and artist affiliation before any collab or likeness use.

Mummers: blackface was banned only in 1964, racist and anti-LGBTQ skits have recurred since, and 'Golden Slippers' is a minstrel-era song. Borrow the craft, not the characters, and vet any tie-in with Black and LGBTQ Philadelphians first.

Third-party IP needs licenses or permission. That covers the PIR catalog and logo, 'TSOP,' 'Ain't No Stoppin' Us Now,' 'Dreams and Nightmares,' Meek's Dreamchasers mark, Sun Ra's name and El Saturn art, the Roots Picnic name, Spectrum branding and SEPTA map art.

Street references: 'P.S.K.' stood for a Parkside gang, and Iverson's rap album as Jewelz was shelved in 2000 over violent and homophobic lyrics. Don't mine either for graphics. Tell Meek's story through his reform advocacy, not prison imagery.

art.headline: Philly invented the tag, then commissioned 4,000-plus murals to say it louder
art.summary: Philadelphia's art is commissioned and handmade at once. Cornbread and Cool Earl were writing on its walls in the late 1960s, and Mural Arts has since put up more than 4,000. After dark the city draws in thin lines of light, from PSFS neon to Boathouse Row. Bring Philly-drawn lettering and outline-light graphics, and skip colonial clichés, the Chinatown arena fight and unlicensed landmark art.

insights.title: Murals are commissioned, block by block
insights.detail: Mural Arts Philadelphia grew out of the 1984 Philadelphia Anti-Graffiti Network under Jane Golden. It now counts more than 4,000 murals, most made through neighborhood meetings where residents shape the image. In Philly a mural reads as a block's civic story more than as rebellion.
insights.implication: Copy the process, not just the look. Hold community design sessions, name a lead muralist who is paid and credited, and leave a wall or court in the neighborhood after the product sells out.

insights.title: The tag was born here, and it is tall
insights.detail: Darryl 'Cornbread' McCray and Cool Earl were writing on Philly walls in the late 1960s. The city's handstyle, 'wickets,' is skinny, condensed and long-stroked. Steve Powers (ESPO) folded that lineage into sign painting with 'A Love Letter for You' (2009), about 50 rooftop murals along the Market-Frankford El between 45th and 63rd Streets in West Philly.
insights.implication: Philly lettering should be vertical and condensed, which suits jersey numerals and chest wordmarks. Have Philly hands from this lineage draw it. Don't pull it from a generic graffiti font.

insights.title: The skyline speaks in single lines of light
insights.detail: Philly draws its night in thin glowing outlines. Boathouse Row's lit boathouses line Kelly Drive. Venturi and Rauch's steel 'ghost structure' of Franklin's house stands at Franklin Court (1976). The Ben Franklin Bridge was lit in 1987. The red neon PSFS letters sit at 12th and Market, and the Divine Lorraine's rooftop sign crowns North Broad.
insights.implication: Line-art outlines, reflective piping and glow trims are the native graphic language. Philadelphia is among the franchises getting Nike's 'Specter' uniforms, and a new arena is rising on the former Spectrum site, so a 'ghost outline' story is timely. Lead with PSFS, Divine Lorraine and Franklin Court, not Boathouse Row, which Philly product has leaned on before.

insights.title: The Workshop of the World still makes cloth
insights.detail: Kensington's mills and North Philly's Stetson hat factory made Philadelphia the 'Workshop of the World.' That lineage lives on at the Fabric Workshop and Museum, where artists have worked in experimental fabric and print since 1977. It also lives at Jefferson University's textile and fashion programs (the former Philadelphia Textile School) and Drexel's Westphal fashion program.
insights.implication: Philly is a credible place for a material-innovation story. Artist-developed prints and knits, co-made with FWM and Jefferson textile students, give a City Edition or retail capsule substance beyond graphics.

insights.title: The art-school map just reshuffled
insights.detail: University of the Arts closed abruptly in June 2024 and PAFA ended its degree programs. That leaves Temple's Tyler School of Art and Architecture, Moore College of Art & Design, Drexel, Jefferson and Penn as the pipeline, plus a large pool of displaced UArts alumni and faculty.
insights.implication: A paid open call or design brief for UArts alumni and Tyler and Moore students would read as real investment in a bruised scene, and it would surface collaborators fast. Avoid anything that looks like free spec work.

insights.title: Arena geography is an art-world flashpoint
insights.detail: From 2022 to January 2025, Chinatown residents, artists and groups led by the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation fought the Sixers' proposed 76 Place arena on Market East. The team instead partnered with Comcast Spectacor on a privately funded arena on the former Spectrum site in South Philly. Renderings were unveiled in September 2026, and completion is reported for 2030.
insights.implication: Keep Chinatown imagery out of Sixers product unless Chinatown artists invite it. Point the arena-era story at the Spectrum site, where Dr. J's 1983 champions played. Public-art commissions for the new building are a long-lead opportunity to track.

insights.title: Black Philly modernism, still under-used
insights.detail: Henry Ossawa Tanner trained at PAFA under Thomas Eakins. Dox Thrash co-invented the carborundum print at the city's WPA Fine Print Workshop. North Philly's Barkley L. Hendricks painted life-size portraits of 1970s Black Philadelphia style. The African American Museum in Philadelphia and Germantown's The Colored Girls Museum carry that lineage forward.
insights.implication: Build February product and Sixers heritage stories with living Black Philly artists, paid and credited. License any Hendricks or Thrash reference through their estates. It is a richer, less-used source than Liberty Bell graphics.

places.name: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
places.why: Isaiah Zagar's mirror-and-tile labyrinth is the hub of the Zagar mosaics on surrounding South Philly walls, the city's most recognizable surface texture.

places.name: A Love Letter for You (Steve Powers)
places.neighborhood: West Philadelphia (Market Street, 45th to 63rd, along the El)
places.why: Sign-painted one-liners seen from the Market-Frankford El. It's the purest example of Philly hand lettering at city scale.

places.name: The Fabric Workshop and Museum
places.why: Since 1977 it has paired artists with fabricators to invent new prints and materials, a natural partner for a Philly material story.

places.name: Taller Puertorriqueño
places.kind: Puerto Rican cultural center and gallery
places.neighborhood: Fairhill, North Philadelphia (El Centro de Oro)
places.why: Since 1974 the anchor of Puerto Rican art and printmaking in North Philly, and the right partner for any Latino-led design story.

places.name: Divine Lorraine
places.neighborhood: North Broad Street at Fairmount Avenue
places.why: Father Divine's racially integrated hotel from 1948, revived as apartments in the mid-2010s. Its rooftop sign is North Broad's signature letterform.

places.name: LOVE Park (JFK Plaza)
places.why: Robert Indiana's LOVE sculpture, plus the granite ledges where Stevie Williams and Ricky Oyola made Philly an East Coast skate capital before the 2002 skate ban.

places.name: Crane Arts
places.why: A converted industrial building with dozens of artist studios and a large project space, and a node of the Kensington-Fishtown maker scene.

places.name: The Colored Girls Museum
places.why: Vashti DuBois's 'memoir museum' in a Germantown house honors the stories of Black girls and women. It is a respected partner for February and women's programming.

places.name: Tyler School of Art and Architecture (Temple University)
places.why: The city's main art-school pipeline after the UArts closure, with graphic design, fibers and material studies a short walk from North Broad.

places.name: We the Youth (Keith Haring mural)
places.neighborhood: Point Breeze, South Philadelphia (22nd and Ellsworth)
places.why: Haring's 1987 mural, painted with neighborhood kids and restored by Mural Arts, proves that pop-art icons live on Philly rowhouse walls.

people.name: Jane Golden
people.role: Founder and executive director, Mural Arts Philadelphia
people.why: She built the anti-graffiti effort into the nation's largest public-art program, and she is the gatekeeper for any community-process mural collaboration.

people.name: Steve Powers (ESPO)
people.role: Philly-born graffiti writer turned sign painter and artist
people.why: He made 'A Love Letter for You' along the El. His hand-painted one-liners are the most Philly typography of a generation and translate directly to tees and walls.

people.name: Darryl 'Cornbread' McCray
people.why: Credited as one of the first modern graffiti writers in the late 1960s, he is a living origin story for Philly lettering. Engage him with pay and credit.

people.name: Isaiah Zagar
people.role: Mosaic artist, founder of Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
people.why: His broken-tile and mirror walls define South Street's texture. Any mosaic cue should go through him or the Magic Gardens.

people.name: Michelle Angela Ortiz
people.why: A Philadelphia artist whose large-scale public work centers immigrant and Latino families, and a credible lead for community-process commissions.

people.name: Stevie Williams
people.role: Pro skateboarder and founder of DGK
people.why: He came up on LOVE Park's ledges and links Philly street style, skate and hip-hop, a credible streetwear voice.

people.name: Barkley L. Hendricks (estate)
people.why: Philadelphia-born and PAFA-trained, he painted 1970s Black cool and is the most fashion-literate painter in the city's canon. Any reference needs estate licensing.

people.name: Mitchell & Ness
people.why: It launched the early-2000s throwback boom from Philly, set local fans' bar for heritage-jersey accuracy, and is Nike's main rival in NBA throwback retail.

moments.name: Mummers Parade
moments.timing: January 1, Broad Street, with the Fancy Brigade finale indoors at the Convention Center
moments.why: The city's biggest costume spectacle: sequins, feathers and satin backpieces built all year in South Philly clubs along Two Street. It is a craft source with a fraught blackface history.

moments.name: Philadelphia Tattoo Arts Convention
moments.timing: Late winter (typically February), Pennsylvania Convention Center
moments.why: The place to scout tattoo artists who already draw Philly lettering and iconography, ideal for a flash-sheet collab.

moments.name: Odunde Festival
moments.timing: Second Sunday of June, South Street around 23rd
moments.why: Founded in 1975 by Lois Fernandez, it is one of the nation's largest African American street festivals and a marketplace of Black and diaspora designers and textile vendors.

moments.name: Philadelphia Open Studio Tours (POST)
moments.why: Hundreds of artists open their studios citywide just as the season tips off, the fastest way to scout collaborators.

moments.name: DesignPhiladelphia
moments.why: A citywide design festival run by the Center for Architecture and Design, and a ready stage for a Nike and Sixers design talk or studio tour near tip-off.

moments.name: First Friday in Old City
moments.timing: First Friday of every month, North 2nd and 3rd Streets
moments.why: Philadelphia's long-running gallery night is a low-cost, recurring way to show a local collab to the art crowd.

vocabulary.meaning: Philly's all-purpose noun for any thing, place or person. Locals love it, but it's worn out on tourist merch, so use it only in a fresh context.
Philly's tall, skinny, long-legged graffiti handstyle, the letterform local writers recognize instantly.
The elevated Market-Frankford Line through West Philly and Kensington. 'Under the El' evokes Kensington Avenue and the Love Letter rooftops.
South 2nd Street in South Philly, home of the Mummers clubs and the New Year's Day after-party.
The Philly pronunciation of water ice. Hand-lettered water-ice signs on corner stands are part of the summer sign vernacular.

The belief that Philly teams lost after One Liberty Place (1987) rose above William Penn's statue on City Hall. It broke in 2007, when ironworkers put a Penn figurine atop the Comcast Center before the Phillies' 2008 title.
'Let brotherly love continue,' the motto on the city's coat of arms and flag.
The industrial-era nickname for Philly's mills and factories, and a heritage line for any made-in-Philly material story.

designCues.cue: Philadelphia flag azure (about #6CA0DC) paired with flag gold (about #F2C230). These are the city's own colors, not the Sixers'.
designCues.source: The city flag, adopted in 1895, whose azure and gold honor the New Sweden colonists. Its coat of arms carries 'Philadelphia Maneto.'
designCues.use: A civic accent for Philly-only product: tonal azure on Sixers navy (#002B5C) or a gold 'Maneto' tag. Don't reproduce the full coat of arms as a logo.

designCues.cue: PSFS neon red (about #E8202A) as a single glowing stroke on black or navy.
designCues.source: The 27-foot red neon PSFS letters atop the 1932 Howe and Lescaze tower at 12th and Market, now the Loews hotel.
designCues.use: Use for piping, outline trims and night-game accents. Borrow the glow and letter spacing, not the PSFS initials, which need clearance.

designCues.cue: Broad Street Line orange (about #F58220), the route color that carries fans from North Philly down Broad to the South Philly sports complex.
designCues.source: SEPTA's color for the Broad Street subway, relettered 'B' in the SEPTA Metro wayfinding rebrand.
designCues.use: A game-day accent or a route-line graphic running North Broad to the arena. Reference the color and route, never SEPTA's logo.

designCues.cue: Ghost outlines: single-weight line drawings of buildings that glow, like Boathouse Row's lights or Franklin Court's steel frame of a house that no longer stands.
designCues.source: Boathouse Row's outline lights, Venturi and Rauch's 1976 Franklin Court ghost structure, the 1987 Ben Franklin Bridge lighting and the vanished Spectrum.
designCues.use: Reflective or glow-in-the-dark line art and piping for a night or Specter-game capsule. A Spectrum-footprint outline bridges the old arena and the new one on the same site.

designCues.cue: Wickets handstyle: tall, condensed letters with long vertical strokes and sharp terminals, plus Steve Powers' sign-painter block letters with drop shadows.
designCues.source: Philly graffiti from Cornbread's era onward, plus the Love Letter rooftops and corner-store hoagie and water-ice signs.
designCues.use: Commission a paid, credited Philly writer or sign painter to draw numerals and wordmarks. Never fake it with an off-the-shelf graffiti font.

designCues.cue: Printer's grotesque: heavy American gothic type in the Franklin Gothic tradition, set tight and all caps.
designCues.source: Franklin Gothic (American Type Founders, 1902) is named for printer Ben Franklin. Philadelphia's Binny and Ronaldson (1796) was America's first lasting type foundry.
designCues.use: A 'set in Philadelphia' typographic story for Philly-only tees and hangtags. License the commercial font or commission a revival.

designCues.cue: Flemish-bond brick: red brick (about #9B4A35) checkered with blue-black glazed header bricks (about #2E3440).
designCues.source: Colonial row houses in Old City and Society Hill, and the date-and-initial patterned brick houses of Salem County in South Jersey.
designCues.use: A jacquard knit, emboss or side-panel texture on warmups and shorts. The narrow trinity row-house silhouette works as a small hangtag icon.

designCues.cue: Fancy-brigade shine: sequin-dense, satin and feathered surfaces in high-saturation color.
designCues.source: Mummers costumes built in South Philly clubhouses for the New Year's Day parade.
designCues.use: Iridescent foil prints or satin warmup panels, made with paid and credited Mummers costume makers. Use the craft only, never Comic or Wench brigade characters.

productHooks: 'Love Letter to Philly' home-opener drop: commission Steve Powers and Philly sign painters to hand-paint one-liners on a wall along the Broad Street Line route. Run the lettering on tees and hoodies for the Cavaliers home opener (James and Brown's Philly debut), and credit the crew on hangtags.

'Ghost Lines' capsule for the Specter games and the Spectrum-site arena story: reflective single-line outlines of the Spectrum, the Divine Lorraine sign and Franklin Court's ghost frame on Sixers navy (#002B5C). Add PSFS-red (#E8202A) piping and Broad Street orange (#F58220) route trims.
Philly wickets type kit: a condensed numeral and wordmark set drawn by a paid Philly handstyle writer. Use it only on Philly-market tees, the team store and Xfinity Mobile Arena retail.

Mural Arts court-and-warmup program: fund a rec-center court and wall in North or West Philly through Mural Arts' community design process. Then turn the finished mural into a limited shooting shirt, with proceeds to Mural Arts youth programs.
Workshop of the World material story: a Fabric Workshop and Museum artist-in-residence and Jefferson textile students co-develop a Flemish-bond brick jacquard for a Philly-only pregame jacket.
watchouts: Landmark art is licensed IP. Robert Indiana's LOVE, the Rocky statue (film IP), Oldenburg's Clothespin, Haring's We the Youth, Zagar's mosaics and every Mural Arts wall (muralist copyright and VARA rights) need clearance before use as graphics or shoot backdrops. The PSFS letters and SEPTA marks are trademarks.

Mummers: blackface was banned in 1964 but has recurred in recent decades, and Comic and Wench brigade caricature still draws protest. Borrow fancy-brigade craft by hiring costume makers. Never borrow the characters or the minstrel-era 'Golden Slippers' anthem.

Chinatown is still raw from the 76 Place fight. Keep Chinatown gates, lanterns and imagery out of Sixers product, and engage Chinatown artists only through groups like Asian Arts Initiative or PCDC, on their terms.
Mural Arts began as the Anti-Graffiti Network, and many writers distrust it. Hire graffiti writers directly, pay and credit them, and never fake tags or glamorize hitting walls Nike does not own.

Cliche fatigue: 'jawn,' Rocky, the Liberty Bell crack and 1776 type saturated the city through the 2026 Semiquincentennial, World Cup matches and MLB All-Star Game. The Sixers' own 13-star identity already covers colonial history. Lead with 20th-century and contemporary Philly instead.

food.headline: Philadelphia eats in code: order "Whiz wit" and skip the Pat's-versus-Geno's duel
food.summary: Philly food is working-class, sandwich-first and argued over, right down to how you order. Locals wear hometown snack brands like team gear, and the new energy comes from immigrant corridors and James Beard-winning chefs. Game day stays at the south end of Broad. That matters, because Chinatown just beat the Sixers' Market East arena plan. Speak the order-counter language, not the cheesesteak clichés.

insights.title: The order is the code, not the sandwich photo
insights.detail: Locals treat Pat's King of Steaks and Geno's at 9th and Passyunk as the tourist answer. The real arguments are neighborhood loyalties: Dalessandro's in Roxborough, John's Roast Pork in Pennsport, Angelo's on 9th Street, Steve's Prince of Steaks in the Northeast and Max's in North Philly from 'Creed.' They also argue about the roll (Amoroso's, Liscio's, Sarcone's seeded). The fastest shibboleth is the order: 'one Whiz wit' means Cheez Whiz with fried onions.
insights.implication: Design around the ordering grammar and the roll, with shorthand typography and seeded texture. Skip cheesesteak illustrations. They read as airport-shop merch to the people Nike most needs to win.

insights.title: Roast pork, the hoagie and tomato pie are the insider flex
insights.detail: DiNic's at Reading Terminal Market and John's Roast Pork (James Beard America's Classic, 2006) made the roast pork Italian, with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. Serious locals rank it above the cheesesteak. The hoagie is just as Philly and far less merchandised. Local legend names it for the Hog Island shipyard, and it became the official sandwich in 1992. Sauce-forward tomato pie from Italian bakeries like Sarcone's is in the same class.
insights.implication: A 'Roast Pork Italian' colorway (rabe green, provolone cream, jus brown) passes the swap test where a generic cheesesteak graphic never will. It tells locals Nike knows the city from the inside.

insights.title: Snack brands are already hometown merch
insights.detail: Tastykake (baked in Philly since 1914) is known for Butterscotch Krimpets and Peanut Butter Kandy Kakes. Wawa has the goose logo, Shorti and Classic hoagies and summer Hoagiefest. Rita's was founded in Bensalem in 1984, Herr's comes from Chester County and Bassetts dates to 1861. With Philly Pretzel Factory, their design languages show up on locals' tees and Halloween costumes. Wawa loyalty, plus pork roll on a kaiser, also ties South Jersey and the suburbs to the city.
insights.implication: These are the market's true cult labels, but every one is third-party IP. Pursue a licensed co-brand, such as a Tastykake or Wawa capsule, or translate the feeling into unbranded cues. Never borrow the marks.

insights.title: Game day stays at the south end of Broad
insights.detail: Pregame means Chickie's & Pete's crab fries with white cheese sauce on Packer Avenue, Tony Luke's on Oregon Avenue and the Xfinity Live! bar complex across from the arena. Across Broad, the FDR Park Southeast Asian Market runs on weekends in the warm months. Cambodian and other Southeast Asian refugee families started it. The privately funded arena rendered in September 2026 for the former Spectrum site keeps the Sixers in this district into the 2030s, though construction may reshape the pregame map.
insights.implication: Show up where fans already eat before tip: Xfinity Live!, Packer Avenue and the FDR market in playoff season. Treat the stadium-district food map, not Center City, as the home-court backdrop for opening-week and playoff drops.

insights.title: Immigrant corridors are the city's current palate
insights.detail: The 9th Street Italian Market is now as Mexican as Italian, anchored by Cristina Martínez's weekend-only South Philly Barbacoa. Washington Avenue carries Vietnamese pho and bánh mì (Pho 75), and Cambodian South Philly clusters near 7th Street. North 5th Street's El Centro de Oro is the Puerto Rican heart. Woodland Avenue in Southwest Philly feeds the Liberian and West African community. West Philly's halal steak shops (Saad's) reflect a large Black Muslim community.
insights.implication: The richest community capsules come from these corridors. Co-create them with the owners, pay them and credit them by name. Don't design an 'international Philly' collage in Portland.

insights.title: Chinatown remembers 76 Place
insights.detail: From 2022 to early 2025 the Sixers pushed 76 Place, an arena at the Fashion District on Chinatown's edge. Residents, businesses and groups such as Asian Americans United and the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation fought it under the banner 'No Arena in Chinatown.' The team dropped it for the South Philly deal with Comcast Spectacor.
insights.implication: Don't use Chinatown's Friendship Gate, food or Lunar New Year imagery as decoration on Sixers-branded product. Any Chinatown moment has to be community-led and paid, and should probably wait until the team has repaired the relationship.

insights.title: Award-winning chefs who speak up
insights.detail: Michael Solomonov is one of the city's credible food voices, with Zahav (James Beard Outstanding Restaurant 2019), Federal Donuts and Laser Wolf. So are Cristina Martínez, an immigrant-workers' advocate and Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic 2022, and Nok Suntaranon of Kalaya in Fishtown, also Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic. Ellen Yin, Outstanding Restaurateur in 2023, rounds out the list. Fishtown and Kensington form the chef-driven cluster, from Pizzeria Beddia to Laser Wolf.
insights.implication: Use chef partnerships for capsules built on a story (opening week, the Christmas trip to Los Angeles, All-Star). Let the chef's own story lead, and have Nike pay and credit. Skip celebrity endorsements.

places.name: Reading Terminal Market
places.why: The city's shared pantry since 1893, home to DiNic's roast pork, Bassetts ice cream and Pennsylvania Dutch stands. It sits beside Chinatown and the Convention Center.

places.name: South 9th Street Italian Market
places.why: An outdoor market of awning-covered stalls, fire barrels, Di Bruno Bros., Sarcone's and Fante's, now layered with Mexican taquerias and bakeries.

places.name: John's Roast Pork
places.why: A shack-style counter since 1930 that many locals name as the best roast pork and cheesesteak in the city. It has James Beard America's Classics recognition.

places.name: Chickie's & Pete's (Packer Avenue)
places.why: The stadium-district bar of the Northeast Philly-born crab-fries brand is the default pre- and post-game stop for all four teams.

places.name: Xfinity Live!
places.why: The pregame and watch-party hub across from the arena, where road playoff games draw crowds.

places.name: FDR Park Southeast Asian Market
places.why: Cambodian, Lao, Thai and Vietnamese vendors have sold grilled skewers, papaya salad and sugarcane juice here for decades, just across Broad Street from the arena.

places.name: South Philly Barbacoa
places.neighborhood: South Philly (9th Street, Italian Market area)
places.why: Cristina Martínez's weekend lamb barbacoa counter is the emblem of Mexican 9th Street and the city's most decorated immigrant kitchen.

places.name: Washington Avenue
places.why: The Vietnamese and Southeast Asian corridor of pho houses (Pho 75), bánh mì bakeries and plaza supermarkets.

places.name: El Centro de Oro (North 5th Street)
places.why: The Puerto Rican commercial heart, where alcapurrias, bacalaítos and pernil are everyday food and community pride is on display.

places.name: Kalaya
places.why: Nok Suntaranon's Southern Thai restaurant grew from a tiny BYOB on 9th Street and is now the flagship of Fishtown's chef-driven scene.

people.name: Michael Solomonov
people.role: Chef and co-founder of CookNSolo with Steven Cook (Zahav, Federal Donuts, Laser Wolf, Dizengoff)
people.why: Philly's most nationally recognized chef. Federal Donuts' fried chicken and donut boxes are a casual local staple.

people.name: Cristina Martínez
people.why: A James Beard Best Chef winner and undocumented-workers' advocate, she embodies the Mexican South Philly that now shares 9th Street with the Italian Market.

people.name: Chutatip 'Nok' Suntaranon
people.why: A James Beard Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic winner whose Fishtown restaurant shows the city's newer immigrant-chef ambition.

people.name: Ellen Yin
people.role: Restaurateur, High Street Hospitality (Fork, High Street)
people.why: Her 2023 James Beard Outstanding Restaurateur award recognized decades of anchoring Old City dining and mentoring the scene.

people.name: Kurt Evans
people.why: His End Mass Incarceration dinners made him North Philly's leading voice on food as Black community organizing.

people.name: Tony Luke Jr.
people.role: Owner of Tony Luke's, Oregon Avenue
people.why: A South Philly roast-pork and steak personality whose original shop sits beside the stadium district.

people.name: Tasty Baking Company (Tastykake)
people.role: Philadelphia snack-cake maker since 1914, now baking at the Navy Yard
people.why: Krimpets and Kandy Kakes are lunchbox nostalgia across the Delaware Valley, and the script logo is a wearable hometown badge.

people.name: Wawa
people.role: Delaware County-based convenience chain, founded as a dairy and first opened as a store in 1964
people.why: The goose, the Shorti and Hoagiefest are regional religion from Philly to South Jersey. Wawa also sponsors the city's July 4 Wawa Welcome America festival.

moments.name: Sixers home opener vs. Cleveland
moments.why: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown's Philly home debut, with a Packer Avenue and Xfinity Live! pregame, is the season's first food-and-fandom window.

moments.name: Lunar New Year in Chinatown
moments.timing: February 6, 2027, with lion dances on Race and 10th Streets
moments.why: It is Chinatown's biggest gathering. After the 76 Place fight, the Sixers can join only through a community-led partnership.

moments.name: Rita's First Day of Spring
moments.why: The free water ice giveaway from the Bensalem-born chain marks the unofficial start of spring. Its lines become a regional ritual just as the playoff race tightens.

moments.name: National Pretzel Day
moments.why: Pennsylvania's pretzel holiday, with free-pretzel lines at Philly Pretzel Factory, lands in the first round of the playoffs.

moments.name: South 9th Street Italian Market Festival
moments.why: Street food, music and vendors along 9th Street make it South Philly's Italian-American and Mexican block party.

moments.name: Odunde Festival
moments.timing: Second Sunday in June, South Street at 23rd
moments.why: Founded in 1975 by Lois Fernandez, it is one of the country's largest African American street festivals and a major showcase for Black food vendors.

moments.name: Wawa Welcome America
moments.why: The city's multi-day Independence festival, with free events and Wawa hoagies, ends with the Parkway concert during free-agency season.

moments.name: Philadelphia Puerto Rican Day Parade and festival
moments.why: It brings the North 5th Street community, its flags and its food to Center City just before training camp.

vocabulary.meaning: The canonical cheesesteak order: Cheez Whiz with fried onions. 'Witout' means no onions.
Never a 'sub.' Philly's official sandwich, usually built on a seeded or Amoroso's roll.
Water ice, Philly's scoopable Italian ice, as locals pronounce it.
The mid-size Wawa hoagie, between Junior and Classic. Ordering one marks you as local.
Chocolate sprinkles on soft-serve or water-ice gelati.
South Philly Italian-American red sauce, as in Sunday gravy.
Tastykake Butterscotch Krimpets, shorthand for Philly lunchbox nostalgia.
Philly's all-purpose noun for any thing, place or event, as in 'that roast pork jawn.'

designCues.cue: Whiz orange: a warm processed-cheese orange used only as a drip or accent hit
designCues.source: The 'Whiz wit' cheesesteak order
designCues.use: Use as tipping, aglets or an inside-collar print against Sixers blue #006BB6. Never use it as a body color, and leave off the Kraft Heinz Cheez Whiz name and jar.

designCues.cue: Broccoli rabe green from the roast pork Italian trio (pair with provolone cream #F1E6C8 and jus brown #6B4226)
designCues.source: DiNic's and John's Roast Pork: roast pork, rabe and sharp provolone
designCues.use: Build an insider three-tone colorway for a lifestyle sneaker or fleece set. Name it for the order, not any shop's brand.

designCues.cue: Cherry water ice red with lemon #F3E58A
designCues.source: The classic cherry and lemon cups from corner water-ice stands and Rita's
designCues.use: Use for a summer, draft or free-agency capsule. Keep the cherry just off Sixers red #ED174C so it reads as seasonal, not as a team color.

designCues.cue: Seeded-roll speckle: dense toasted sesame seeds on a golden crust
designCues.source: Sarcone's-style seeded hoagie and steak rolls from Italian Market bakeries
designCues.use: Render as a speckled outsole, a heathered knit or a printed liner, a nod only locals will clock.

designCues.cue: Pretzel strip: figure-eight Philly soft pretzels baked fused side by side and sold in ribbons, with coarse salt
designCues.source: Corner pretzel bakeries and the street-corner vendor bag
designCues.use: Use as a repeating knotted pattern on socks and liners, or as salt-crystal flecks. Or package five-pack socks as a 'strip' in a brown paper bag.

designCues.cue: Butcher-paper wrap marked in grease pencil with order shorthand ('WIZ WIT,' 'PROV,' 'X HOT')
designCues.source: How steak shops and hoagie counters label wrapped orders
designCues.use: Use for tissue paper, hangtags, inside-label prints and box liners. Have a Philly letterer draw the type instead of using a stock marker font.

designCues.cue: Fluted paper water-ice cup: tight vertical pleats and a rolled rim
designCues.source: Water-ice stands from South Philly to South Jersey
designCues.use: Translate into ribbed knit cuffs, pleated trims or cup-shaped limited packaging for the summer capsule.

designCues.cue: Hog Island hoagie story: the sandwich supposedly named for World War I shipyard workers at Hog Island, now the site of the airport
designCues.source: Local origin lore behind the city's official sandwich
designCues.use: Use for a hangtag or campaign line about work-shift food and blue-collar Philly. Label it as legend, not fact.

productHooks: 'WIT / WITOUT' home-debut pack for the James-Brown opener against Cleveland: tees and hoodies set in order-shorthand typography, with Whiz-orange hits and butcher-paper packaging. LeBron is the roster's Nike asset, so it can be his Philly welcome.

'Roast Pork Italian' colorway (rabe green, provolone cream, jus brown) on a LeBron lifestyle silhouette or a fleece set. Launch it with a paid tasting at a roast-pork counter, not at a tourist steak corner.
National Pretzel Day playoff drop (April 26): five-pack socks sold as a 'strip' in a brown paper pretzel bag, with a salt-speck knit and a figure-eight graphic. Release it during the first round.
Water-ice summer capsule (cherry and lemon, fluted-cup ribbing), teased on Rita's First Day of Spring and released around the draft. Ideally make it a licensed Rita's collab.

Paid, co-credited neighborhood capsules with immigrant-corridor businesses: South Philly Barbacoa, a Washington Avenue bakery, the FDR Park Southeast Asian Market vendors across from the arena. Share proceeds and let each business tell its story in its own words.
Licensed nostalgia collab with Tastykake (Krimpet butterscotch) or Wawa (Hoagiefest) for a holiday or Christmas-in-L.A. drop. Price it as fan gear, not hype resale.
watchouts: Third-party IP needs licensing: Cheez Whiz (Kraft Heinz), Tastykake (Flowers Foods), Wawa's name and goose, Rita's, Herr's, Philly Pretzel Factory and Chickie's & Pete's trademarked Crabfries. Use unbranded sensory cues unless a deal is signed.

Pat's versus Geno's is the tourist cliché, and Geno's carries baggage from its 'speak English' sign (removed in 2016). Steer away from it as a partner. Remember too that Joe's Steaks renamed itself in 2013 to drop a slur.
Chinatown is off-limits as Sixers decoration after the 76 Place arena fight. Engage only through Chinatown-led groups, and do not frame any Chinatown work as arena marketing.

Immigrant and Black Muslim food traditions (barbacoa, Cambodian market stalls, halal steaks, bean pies) belong to their communities. Partner, pay and credit. Never use religious imagery or a chef's immigration story without explicit consent.
Philadelphia Cream Cheese is a Kraft brand with no Philly roots, and locals mock its use as a city signifier. Keep it out.

culture.headline: Philly is the overlooked city that reps by the block, and it likes it that way
culture.summary: Outsiders picture Rocky, a booed Santa and thrown batteries. Philadelphia answers: "No one likes us, we don't care." Pride runs local, from the 215 to Delco, the Main Line and South Jersey. The city adopts outsiders who grind and turns on stars who seem not to care, and that is the 2026-27 test for LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

insights.title: No one likes us, we don't care
insights.detail: Locals know the caricature: Santa pelted with snowballs at Franklin Field in 1968, batteries, greased light poles. They answer with defiant loyalty. "No one likes us, we don't care" started as a Millwall chant. Jason Kelce turned it into a civic creed in his 2018 parade speech, delivered in a Mummers outfit. The Eagles' Super Bowl LIX parade in February 2025 revived it. The chip is about respect and effort, not chaos, and Philly boos its own when the effort isn't there.
insights.implication: Talk the way locals talk about themselves: effort and accountability. Skip "crazy fans" gags, which sound like outsiders laughing at the city. Never look like a brand pretending to be from here.

insights.title: Adopted sons earn it; passengers get booed
insights.detail: The city made heroes of outsiders who ground it out: Allen Iverson from Hampton, Va., Kelce from Cleveland, Jimmy Butler after one season. It turned on stars who seemed checked out, like Ben Simmons and James Harden. Jaylen Brown arrives from the Celtics, whom the Sixers beat in the 2026 first round after trailing 3-1. LeBron James is 41 and turns 42 in December.
insights.implication: Pitch the James and Brown debuts as "earn Philly," not superteam glamour. Product released after real milestones will land better than preseason hype. LeBron is a lifetime Nike athlete, so the most direct play is a Philly-specific LeBron colorway for his home debut against Cleveland.

insights.title: Defend the building against New York
insights.detail: Knicks fans took over Philadelphia's arena during the 2024 playoffs. That pushed the team to limit playoff ticket sales to the region, and ownership to buy up seats for local fans. The Knicks swept the Sixers in the 2026 second round and won the title. They host Philadelphia on ring night to open the season on Oct 20.
insights.implication: Sell a Philly-first drop to Delaware Valley ZIP codes first, timed to the Knicks' first visit to Philadelphia. It turns a real grievance into a home-court product story.

insights.title: A basketball city under a football town
insights.detail: Fall Sundays belong to the Eagles, but the basketball lineage runs deeper. It takes in the Palestra, the Big 5, the Public and Catholic League rivalries and summer pro-am lore. A line runs from Wilt Chamberlain (Overbrook) and Earl Monroe (Bartram) to Dawn Staley (North Philly) and Kobe Bryant (Lower Merion). Nike already makes the Eagles' uniforms, so it works both sides of the city's calendar.
insights.implication: Earn grassroots credibility through rec-center courts, the Public League and Big 5 moments. Save the loudest Sixers drops for gaps in the Eagles schedule and for after football ends in January or February.

insights.title: People rep blocks and area codes, not the skyline
insights.detail: Inside the 215/267/445, people name South Philly, North Philly, West Philly, Germantown, Fishtown or "the Northeast" first. The 610/484 suburbs (Delco, Montco, the Main Line) and the 856 in South Jersey are a running argument: do they count as "Philly"? The Sixers train in Camden, which complicates the debate.
insights.implication: Build modular local product: neighborhood and area-code editions, each designed by artists from that place. Skip the one Center City skyline graphic. Include the suburbs and South Jersey without pretending they're the city.

insights.title: Back to the Spectrum site, after the Chinatown fight
insights.detail: From 2022 to 2025 the team pushed its 76 Place arena on Market East, against sustained opposition from Chinatown groups. It dropped the plan in January 2025. The new arena with Comcast Spectacor goes back to the Spectrum site, home of Dr. J and Moses Malone's 1983 champions. It will also house Philadelphia's WNBA team.
insights.implication: "Back to the Spectrum" is a heritage story locals will welcome, but the team and Comcast should announce it. Keep Chinatown out of any arena stories unless Chinatown partners shape it.

insights.title: After the 250th, retire the 1776 clichés
insights.detail: The franchise's name came from a 1963 fan contest honoring 1776. Summer 2026 filled the city with Semiquincentennial Liberty Bell and founding imagery, on top of World Cup matches and the MLB All-Star Game. Locals have other civic symbols: Penn's five-square grid, Billy Penn atop City Hall, the blue-and-gold city flag and the motto "Philadelphia maneto."
insights.implication: Lead 2026-27 graphics with those civic, non-colonial symbols. Make the pregame Liberty Bell ring a game-night moment, not a print.

places.name: The Palestra
places.why: Penn's 1927 "Cathedral of College Basketball" is the spiritual home of the Big 5 and the city's hoops memory.

places.name: South Philadelphia Sports Complex (Broad and Pattison)
places.why: All four teams play here, tailgate culture rules, and the former Spectrum site is where the next Sixers arena will rise.

places.name: Broad Street (City Hall to Pattison Avenue)
places.why: The city's celebration spine. Fans flood it after titles, championship parades run down it, and the Broad Street Line carries them to games.

places.name: Italian Market (South 9th Street)
places.why: The old Italian outdoor market is now just as much Calle Nueve, the Mexican South Philly corridor. It is a living map of the city's immigrant layers.

places.name: Two Street (South 2nd Street)
places.why: Home of the Mummers clubhouses and the New Year's Day street party, and the heart of white working-class South Philly identity.

places.name: El Centro de Oro (North 5th Street)
places.why: The "Golden Block" is the commercial corridor of Philadelphia's Puerto Rican community, one of the largest on the mainland.

places.name: Chinatown Friendship Gate (10th and Arch)
places.why: Symbol of the neighborhood that led the fight against the 76 Place arena. A reminder that the Sixers brand carries history here.

places.name: Johnson House Historic Site
places.why: An Underground Railroad station on Germantown Avenue, part of the deep civic and Black history Germantown residents rep.

places.name: Philadelphia 76ers Training Complex
places.why: The team trains on the Camden waterfront and keeps its Legends Walk of former stars there. That makes South Jersey part of the team's home.

places.name: Lower Merion High School (Bryant Gymnasium)
places.why: Kobe Bryant's high school gym, named for him, ties a Nike icon to the Philadelphia suburbs.

people.name: Julius Erving (Dr. J)
people.why: The defining Sixer of the Spectrum era. His Converse Pro Leather years give Nike a family-owned heritage link.

people.name: Allen Iverson
people.why: The adopted son who proved effort beats size. Still the city's emotional touchstone, but a Reebok lifer.

people.name: Wilt Chamberlain (estate)
people.role: Hall of Famer, Overbrook High alum
people.why: West Philly's giant scored 100 for the Philadelphia Warriors in 1962 and led the 68-13 champion Sixers in 1967.

people.name: Kobe Bryant (estate)
people.role: Philadelphia-born Hall of Famer, Lower Merion alum
people.why: Philly booed him as a Laker, then mourned him as its own. His signature line is Nike's, and his estate must approve.

people.name: Dawn Staley
people.role: South Carolina head coach, Olympic champion
people.why: A North Philly legend from the Raymond Rosen homes, and the obvious cultural bridge to Philadelphia's WNBA future.

people.name: Jason Kelce
people.why: He gave the city its "No one likes us" parade speech in a Mummers outfit. The model of an outsider who became Philly.

people.name: Meek Mill
people.why: "Dreams and Nightmares" is the city's walk-out anthem, and his justice-reform work keeps him tied to the neighborhoods.

people.name: Kevin Hart
people.why: A courtside regular who carries the city's chip-on-the-shoulder humor to a national audience.

moments.name: Mummers Parade
moments.timing: January 1, Broad Street, then Two Street
moments.why: The city's oldest folk ritual: sequins, feathers and the "Golden Slippers" strut. It has a painful blackface history to navigate.

moments.name: MLK Day of Service
moments.why: Philadelphia runs one of the country's largest MLK service days. The Sixers are in Atlanta that afternoon, so local work stands on its own.

moments.name: Penn Relays
moments.timing: Last weekend of April, Franklin Field
moments.why: The country's oldest relay meet (1895) draws huge Jamaican and Caribbean crowds. It is a moment of diaspora pride.

moments.name: Odunde Festival
moments.timing: Second Sunday in June, South Street at 23rd
moments.why: Lois Fernandez founded it in 1975. It is one of the country's largest African American street festivals and a Black Philly homecoming.

moments.name: Philly Pride
moments.why: The city that added black and brown stripes to the rainbow flag in 2017 celebrates in a neighborhood with rainbow street signs.

moments.name: Wawa Welcome America
moments.timing: Late June through July 4, Benjamin Franklin Parkway
moments.why: The city's Independence Day festival and free Parkway concert, the summer civic peak.

moments.name: Puerto Rican Day Parade
moments.why: North Philly's Puerto Rican community at its most visible, with flags across Fairhill and Kensington.

moments.name: Big 5 Classic
moments.why: Penn, Temple, La Salle, St. Joe's and Villanova (guest teams vary) in one day of city college hoops. The basketball city in a single building.

vocabulary.meaning: An all-purpose noun for a thing, place, event or person ("that jawn was crazy"). It comes from Black Philly speech and is now used citywide.
Acting out of line or ridiculous ("you drawlin'"). Said when someone says something absurd, like doubting Maxey.
A guy or dude ("that bol nice"), common in North and West Philly.
How much of the city and Delco says "water." It is shorthand for the accent, as in "wooder ice."
Plural "you," heard most in South Philly, the Northeast and Delco.
Going to the Jersey Shore, never "the beach." Shore locals call Philly day-trippers "shoobies."
The Eagles greeting that doubles as hello, goodbye and thank you, all year and in every sport's crowd.
The Sam Hinkie-era rebuild mantra became Joel Embiid's nickname and a chant. It is said with hope or irony, depending on his health.

designCues.cue: Penn's five-square grid: a fine line grid from river to river, with Centre Square (City Hall) in the middle and Rittenhouse, Washington, Franklin and Logan squares around it.
designCues.source: Thomas Holme's 1683 plan of the city for William Penn, still the bones of Center City.
designCues.use: Print it all over shooting shirts and warmup linings, with Centre Square filled in Sixers royal. The historic map is public domain.

designCues.cue: Area-code numerals: 215, 267, 445, 610, 484 and 856 set in heavy athletic block numbers.
designCues.source: 215 dates to the original 1947 area codes. Locals use the codes to say where they're from and to argue about who counts as Philly.
designCues.use: Put the numerals on the backs of tees and hoodies, one edition per code. Print them on the hangtag of every local item.

designCues.cue: "Philadelphia maneto" set in a small engraved serif.
designCues.source: The motto on the city seal, Latin for "let brotherly love continue," and the root of the nickname.
designCues.use: Use it as inner neck tape, waistband or tongue print. It is an insider detail that replaces "City of Brotherly Love" slogans.

designCues.cue: Billy Penn's hat: a tiny silhouette of the Calder statue on top of City Hall.
designCues.source: The Curse of Billy Penn: no titles after One Liberty Place rose above the statue in 1987. Ironworkers put a Penn figurine on the Comcast Center in 2007, and the Phillies won in 2008.
designCues.use: Hide it on hangtags, socks or jock tags as a good-luck charm for the playoff run. The 1890s statue is public domain.

designCues.cue: Wissahickon schist gray, about #6E675C, a heathered gray-brown with a mica glint.
designCues.source: The flecked local stone of Germantown, Mount Airy and Chestnut Hill houses, quarried from the Wissahickon Valley.
designCues.use: Use speckled fleece or a knit with a metallic fleck for a Germantown and Northwest edition, in place of generic charcoal.

designCues.cue: Sixers royal, about #006BB6, paired with Sixers red, about #ED174C, as the lead colors.
designCues.source: In Philly, colors are allegiances: green is the Eagles, orange the Flyers, red and powder blue the Phillies, and royal the Sixers.
designCues.use: Lead every neighborhood and area-code piece with royal so it reads as Sixers at a glance. Avoid green- or orange-led palettes that read as another team.

designCues.cue: Ben Franklin Bridge cable curve as a single continuous line.
designCues.source: The suspension bridge from Old City to Camden, where the Sixers train. PATCO commuters cross it daily, and its cables are lit at night.
designCues.use: Draw one line connecting "215" and "856" on a Philly-South Jersey edition, so the region reads as one fan base without blurring the difference.

designCues.cue: More Color, More Pride: the rainbow flag with black and brown stripes added.
designCues.source: Philadelphia added the two stripes in 2017 to center Black and brown LGBTQ+ people, and the version spread worldwide.
designCues.use: For June, co-design with Philadelphia LGBTQ+ organizations such as the William Way LGBT Community Center. Credit the flag's Philly origin and route proceeds to them.

productHooks: Area Code capsule: a 215/267/445 core with 610/484 and 856 editions, Sixers-royal numerals and a Penn-grid lining. Sell it first to Delaware Valley ZIP codes in the week the Knicks first visit Philadelphia.

LeBron Philly colorway for his home debut against Cleveland, in Sixers royal and red with a "maneto" tongue print and a Billy Penn heel detail. Lead with LeBron and team product, since Brown is not a Nike athlete (verify).

"Back to the Spectrum" heritage warmup, plus a Converse Pro Leather in Sixers colors honoring the Dr. J era (Converse is Nike-owned). Get approval from the team, Comcast Spectacor and Erving, and time it to arena milestones and Specter-uniform games.

Neighborhood Courts pack: tees for South, North and West Philly, Germantown, Fishtown, the Northeast and Camden, each designed with an artist from that place. Release one neighborhood per month. Proceeds rebuild Philadelphia Parks & Recreation courts, such as Hank Gathers Rec Center in North Philly.

"Earn It" tees: limited drops that release only after real milestones, such as the first win over the Knicks, Brown's Jan 21 return to Boston or clinching a playoff spot. Write the effort-first copy with Philly voices.
Community calendar capsules, co-created and credited: Odunde in June, the Puerto Rican Day Parade in September and the MLK Day of Service in January. Name and pay the partner organizations.
watchouts: Chinatown: the 2022-25 fight over the 76 Place arena is fresh. Avoid Chinatown and Lunar New Year imagery (the Friendship Gate, dragons) unless groups like the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation and Asian Americans United are partners. Keep arena stories out of the neighborhood.

Mummers: blackface was banned in 1964 but has resurfaced in incidents since. Send any Mummers or "Golden Slippers" nod through clubs with clean records. Avoid comic-brigade and wench-brigade caricature.

Third-party IP: Rocky and the statue (Amazon MGM), LOVE (Robert Indiana estate), Gritty (Flyers / Comcast Spectacor), the Phanatic (Phillies), Eagles and NFL marks, the "Fresh Prince" theme, Wawa and Tastykake. "Trust the Process" (Embiid) and local slogans such as "Philly vs. Everybody" may be trademarked.

Brand conflicts: Iverson is a Reebok lifer. Mitchell & Ness (founded in Philly, Fanatics-linked) owns the throwback lane. Embiid moved to Skechers, and Brown turned down a reported $50M Nike offer to launch his own 741 shoe brand. Don't build hero product around non-Nike faces.

Credit the communities behind the culture: "jawn," "bol" and "drawlin'" come from Black Philly speech, and "ock" and the Philly beard from its Black Muslim community. Partner with and pay creators from those communities. Never use religious imagery, keep Lenape imagery off product without Lenape partners, and skip the booed-Santa and greased-pole caricature.

underground.headline: Philly's underground runs on banned granite, North Philly stables and sparring gyms
underground.summary: Philly's strongest scenes are street skating, hardcore, North Philly's Black horsemen, ballroom and boxing's "gym wars." The Sixers have an underground too: Process diehards, podcasters and bootleg-tee makers. They will judge the LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era faster than any campaign. Hardcore's sportswear crossover, North Philly Western wear and the new WNBA team are the open doors.

insights.title: LOVE Park made Philly an East Coast skate capital
insights.detail: From the early 1990s until the city's 2002 ban, LOVE Park's granite ledges made stars of Stevie Williams, Ricky Oyola and Josh Kalis. Williams went on to found DGK. Planner Ed Bacon skated the park at 92 in protest, and the city turned down DC Shoes' $1 million offer to keep it open. The scene moved to Paine's Park on the Schuylkill (2013) and the DIY concrete of FDR Skatepark under I-95. Its look is DGK's oversized, hip-hop cut, not California thrash.
insights.implication: Skate is Nike's most credible door here. Go through Nike SB, with skaters from the LOVE and Paine's lineage, and put real money into Franklin's Paine Skatepark Fund. Cut Sixers product for skaters big and hip-hop, not Portland workwear.

insights.title: Philly hardcore already moshes in basketball gear
insights.detail: This Is Hardcore, the summer festival held in Philadelphia since the mid-2000s, anchors the scene. Bands like Soul Glo, Jesus Piece and Mannequin Pussy make the city a national hardcore and punk hub. Crowds two-step in mesh shorts, oversized jerseys over thermals and running shoes. Bands sell custom jerseys as merch.
insights.implication: This crowd ignores team-store product but already wears the silhouette. A boxier Sixers "show jersey," made with a Philly band (licensed and paid), reaches a style-leading audience that mainstream hoops marketing misses.

insights.title: Fletcher Street's Black cowboys had the Western look first
insights.detail: Black horsemen have kept stables around Fletcher Street in North Philadelphia for generations. The Fletcher Street Urban Riding Club teaches neighborhood kids to ride and care for horses. Netflix's Concrete Cowboy (2021, with Idris Elba) put real riders on screen. They ride in hoodies, fitted caps and work boots with saddle leather, a mix that predates the 2024 Western-wear wave.
insights.implication: This is the market's most original style story, and it belongs to the riders. Design any capsule with the club, cast its riders instead of models, and fund the stables, which have fought for years to secure a permanent home.

insights.title: Philly made the Pride flag Black and brown
insights.detail: In June 2017, after a 2016 reckoning over racism in Gayborhood bars, the city's Office of LGBT Affairs added black and brown stripes to the rainbow flag. The design now flies worldwide. Philly Black Pride anchors a ballroom scene of Black and Latino houses. Landmarks include Giovanni's Room, the oldest LGBTQ bookstore in the U.S. (founded 1973, now run by Philly AIDS Thrift), and Bob & Barbara's long-running drag night.
insights.implication: Philly gives Nike's Be True program a real origin story, but only if Black and brown LGBTQ Philadelphians co-create the product. Time it to Black Pride in spring as well as June, and pay and credit the ballroom talent.

insights.title: "Gym wars" beat the Rocky steps
insights.detail: Philadelphia boxing is known for "gym wars," sparring fought at full intensity. The culture runs from Joe Frazier's North Broad gym (closed, but on the National Register) through Front Street Gym to today's Jaron "Boots" Ennis. Club cards at the 2300 Arena, the former ECW Arena where 1990s hardcore wrestling was born, keep the fight-night scene alive.
insights.implication: "Gym wars" is a ready story for Sixers training gear in a season of maximum pressure on Nick Nurse and an aging core. Think heavyweight fleece, reinforced seams and a working gym's co-sign. That way Nike owns Philly toughness without licensing Rocky.

insights.title: The Sixers' own underground wrote "Trust the Process"
insights.detail: During Sam Hinkie's 2013-16 rebuild, Sixers Twitter, the Liberty Ballers blog and The Rights to Ricky Sanchez podcast turned "Trust the Process" into a creed. That was before Joel Embiid took it as a nickname. Fans printed their own shirts ("Hinkie Died for Your Sins"). The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era brings a 41-year-old star and a former Celtic. It will test that crowd's loyalty and irony, and bootleg tees will answer every win and loss within hours.
insights.implication: Win this crowd with speed and self-awareness. Make quick-turn, one-color tees co-signed with fan creators, and product that honors the Process lineage around Embiid. Skip a polished LeBron-first launch. They will mock it.

insights.title: Sons of Ben is the template for Philly's WNBA team
insights.detail: Soccer fans founded the Sons of Ben in 2007, before the Union existed, and helped win the MLS franchise. They still lead the River End at Subaru Park in Chester with tifo, scarves and chants. Philadelphia's WNBA team, due in 2030 in the new South Philly arena, has no supporters' culture yet.
insights.implication: As the WNBA's uniform partner, Nike can help a founding supporters' group form now, with scarves, tifo kits and pre-launch "founder" gear. Borrow the Sons of Ben model. Union kits are Adidas, so copy the playbook, not the club.
